page: Google Cloud Platform n4a-highcpu-8 is an arm64-based virtual machine instance within Google Cloud's general-purpose series, tailored for compute-focused configurations. The system provides 8 dedicated virtual CPU cores paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It operates on an Arm architecture rather than traditional x86 instructions and does not feature hardware-accelerated coprocessors such as GPUs.

Storage and network provisioning rely entirely on external cloud resources, as the instance includes no integrated local NVMe or SSD storage and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Persistent disk configurations and network egress must be connected separately via Google Cloud services. This lean hardware baseline targets workloads that require compute throughput without the overhead of massive memory footprints or attached local scratch storage.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation makes n4a-highcpu-8 suited for compute-bound parallel workloads. Practical applications include batch data transformation, code compilation pipelines, build agents, and distributed web serving clusters where memory consumption per thread is low and Arm compatibility is supported.
description: Google Cloud Platform n4a-highcpu-8 is a compute-focused instance configuration featuring 8 dedicated arm64 virtual CPU cores and 16.0 GB of system memory. Operating at a ratio of 2.0 GB of memory per core, this virtual machine emphasizes CPU density for tasks requiring parallel execution on Arm architecture. The configuration does not include local disk storage, requiring network-attached storage for stateful workloads, nor does it incorporate graphics accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Its hardware distribution supports workloads where computation demands outpace memory usage, delivering resource efficiency for lightweight distributed workers, code compilation, continuous integration and continuous deployment pipelines, and stateless web application hosting.
